newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian unveils plan to stem losses.
newsitem.headline: Canadian unveils plan to stem losses.

text.p: Struggling Canadian Airlines Corp, struggling for survival amid heavy losses, said on Friday it would add transborder capacity, seek wage cuts from employees and ask for concessions from U.S. shareholder AMR Corp.

Canadian, which said its year-to-date financial results were much worse than expected, said it could face a cash crunch in the first quarter of 1997 and that continued losses threatened its viability.
Canadian, which has not posted an annual profit this decade, said it lost $49 million ($36.7 million) in the first nine months of 1996 versus a year earlier loss of C$65.4 million ($49.1 million).

The carrier said it had C$110.8 million ($92.1 million) of cash on hand at the end of the third quarter. But continued operating losses and high debt repayments in the next six months could wipe out reserves.

Canadian said its proposed restructing would involve increased service to the United States and Asia and an 11 percent drop in domestic capacity. It said up to 250 jobs would be eliminated under the plan and that it would ask employees to take a 10 percent wage cut.
Minority shareholder, AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, said on Friday it remained committed to its stake in Canada but did not plan any further investment in the ailing carrier.
